bound_context.question: What does the 84-byte leaf routine at 0x5d0ed60 return for a byte string, a bit offset and a bit width, and what do its callers depend on?

environment_limits: Static disassembly only (objdump/readelf on the digest-verified local binary); no cargo/rustc, Ghidra or a live node; the model is a Python transcription, not a build of node or blst.
ledger: cases.tsv (300 reviewable cases, 75 per family); the full 2,400-case sweep and a 200,000-input differential are re-derived in memory by the tests

observations.text: From the disassembly: rdi=w (byte string), rsi=bitpos, rdx=nbits; the result is returned in rax.
first = bitpos>>3; span = ((bitpos+nbits-1)>>3) - first. rsi holds the negated span and is counted up to zero.
The loop runs exactly four times (add $0x8,%ecx against cmp $0x20,%ecx) and shifts each byte by 8*j, so at most 32 bits are shifted in.
sar $0x3f of the previous rsi yields an all-ones mask while rsi<0 and zero afterwards, so only the span+1 spanned bytes OR into the accumulator; bytes past the field contribute zero.
shr $0x3f,%rdx / add %rdx,%rdi advance the pointer by one only while rsi<0, so the j-th contributing byte is w[first+j].
The final and $0x7,%ecx / shr %cl,%rax drops the bitpos&7 low bits.
No mask-to-nbits instruction exists: the result is the whole spanned window and can carry up to seven extra high bits (get_wval_limb(b'\xa5',0,4)==0xA5 while the 4-bit field is 0x05).
result == (little-endian window of the span+1 spanned bytes) >> (bitpos&7); cross-checked against a literal transcription of the register dance on the 2,400-case sweep and 200,000 random inputs.

All 10 call sites mask the returned window before using it as a field: 2 as their first use (and rax,[rbp-0x80]) and 8 within three instructions of shl rax,cl (and rax,<mask>). The contract is a window holding the requested field in its low bits.

The four caller FDEs (0x5d18160, 0x5d1bf90, 0x5d1c4b0, 0x5d1e410) are blst's windowed scalar-multiplication loops, inferred from the region and the recoding shape; the pinned facts are the call sites, their FDE bounds and their first-use consumers.

unknowns: The C-level meaning of nbits given that the routine never masks to it; the observable behaviour is pinned, the crate-level intent is not.

Fields spanning more than four bytes would be truncated by the 32-bit loop; whether any caller asks for one is not established (bitpos and nbits are runtime values at every call site), so the case is not characterized.
How each caller uses the masked field beyond the first two instructions.
The body is byte-identical in 12 identical source objects; only 0x5d0ed60 is bound.
